paper_title: Thinking Slow, Fast Scaling Inference Compute with Distilled Reasoners
caption: : Majority voting.
model_annotation: This plot illustrates majority voting accuracy as a function of the number of completions (k). The x-axis represents the number of completions (k) on a logarithmic scale (base 2), ranging from 2^0 (1) to 2^8 (256), with tick labels at each power of 2. The y-axis represents majority voting accuracy on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 0.25 to 0.60. There are three lines in the plot. The first line, shown in dark blue with circle markers and a solid style, starts at approximately 0.43 at k=1 and increases gradually, reaching approximately 0.61 at k=256, with a relatively steady upward trend that begins to plateau around k=64. The second line, shown in green with triangle markers and a solid style, starts at approximately 0.26 at k=1 and rises steeply between k=2 and k=16, reaching approximately 0.56 at k=16, then continues to increase more gradually to approximately 0.61 at k=256. The third line, shown in light green/cyan with triangle markers and a solid style, starts at approximately 0.26 at k=1 and increases slowly, reaching approximately 0.45 at k=256, showing a more gradual and modest upward trend compared to the other two lines.
